Ark Start Brunel Nursery
North Kensington nursery
We are very pleased that Ark Start, Ark’s nursery programme, is now operating from Ark Brunel Academy.
✔️ Children from 9 months old are eligible
✔️ 15 or 30 hours per week funded childcare available for 2 and 3 year olds
✔️ Places available all year round or just during school term time
✔️ Flexible booking: 9am to 12pm, 12pm to 3pm or 8am to 5pm.
✔️ You can apply at any point in the year
Our nursery is about much more than childcare
Ark Start was set up by a group of qualified educators passionate about ensuring that every child has access to an excellent early years education and that families have access to flexible and affordable childcare.
Our team ensures every child has a joyful, engaging and secure nursery experience and leaves us ready to start school happily and confidently.
Fully qualified early years educators
Our nursery staff are fully trained and qualified as educators, expert in delivering the government's Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum.
Learning and exploring outside
Our nursery has a large and specially designed outdoor area. Children benefit from stimulating outdoor learning, where they are supported to explore nature and develop their movement skills.
Curriculum designed by specialists
Our early years curriculum is structured around storytelling, encouraging children to tell their own stories and listen to others' stories.
FAQs
Each session at Ark Start is a 3-hour block of time and we are open for 3 sessions per day:
(it is only possible to book 3 hours as 1 session – they can’t be booked separately)
Please see the full guide from Ark Start here
The date you can start accessing free childcare depends on your child’s birthday. Childcare works in terms. There are three terms in a year starting in January, April and September.
1 September - 31 December
1 January – 31 March
You need to have successfully applied before the next term starts. If you miss the deadline, you need to wait until the next term even if your child is eligible to have started. You are able to apply 16 weeks (approx 3 and a half months) before your child’s birthday.
It is encouraged to apply early to ensure your application is approved in time. The government suggests applying at least one month before the deadline.
Morning – 9am to 12pm
Afternoon – 12pm to 3pm
How to apply
If you are interested in applying to our nursery, please visit the Ark Start nursery web page.

Welcome to Ark Brunel
Welcome to Ark Brunel Primary Academy. Ark Brunel Primary Academy is a vibrant school and ambitious school at the heart of our diverse North Kensington community. Our children are at the centre of everything we do, and we are committed to giving every child the very best start in life.
We want every child at Ark Brunel to thrive: academically, socially and personally. We believe that every child has the potential to achieve great things, and we encourage them to choose brilliance in all that they do. Our values of honesty, enthusiasm, ambition, resilience and thought are central to life at our school. They help to shape not only how our children learn, but also the kind of people we are.
As Headteacher, I am committed to creating a school where children feel happy, safe and known; where they are inspired by their learning and supported to aim high. I also believe that a successful school is built on strong relationships between children, families and staff. By working together, we can ensure that every child is given the opportunity to flourish.
We are proud to be part of the Ark Schools network, a leading education charity with a shared mission to transform lives through education. Being part of Ark gives our children and staff access to expertise, opportunities and resources from across a wider family of schools. From Year 5 onwards, every pupil receives a Chromebook, helping them to develop the skills and independence they need to continue their learning beyond the classroom.
Learning at Ark Brunel extends far beyond the school day. Our children can take part in a wide range of enrichment and after-school activities, including arts and crafts, chess, dance and football. We believe these experiences are an important part of a rich and rounded education, allowing children to discover new interests, develop their talents and build confidence.
Great schools are built by great people. We are proud of our dedicated staff and are committed to investing in their development so that our children benefit from excellent teaching and support every day.
I am incredibly excited to lead Ark Brunel and to work alongside our wonderful children, families, staff and wider community. I hope this website gives you a sense of our school and all that we have to offer. If you would like to know more, please do get in touch.
I look forward to welcoming you to Ark Brunel.
Choose brilliance
Our HEART values underpin all our behaviour and interactions with one another, and create an environment where we can all excel. They bind us together and are central to making our goals a reality. They are explicitly taught as part of every child's journey through our school.

Welcome to Personal, Social, Health and Emotional Education (PSHE)
Why PSHE?
At Ark Brunel Primary, we teach Personal, Social, Health Education as a whole-school approach to underpin children’s development as people and because we believe that this also supports their learning capacity. Here, at Ark Brunel Primary we value PSHE as one way to support children’s development as human beings, to enable them to understand and respect who they are, to empower them with a voice and to equip them for life and learning. We include the statutory Relationships and Health Education within our whole-school PSHE Programme
Our approach
To ensure progression and a spiral curriculum, we use Jigsaw, the mindful approach to PSHE, as our chosen teaching and learning programme and tailor it to your children’s needs. Learning is divided into six whole school ‘puzzles’, which are explored in more depth each year, building upon previous learning.
At Ark Brunel Primary we allocate 1 hour to PSHE each week in order to teach the PSHE knowledge and skills in a developmental and age-appropriate way. These explicit lessons are reinforced and enhanced in many ways: Assemblies, praise and reward system, through relationships child to child, adult to child and adult to adult across the school. We aim to ‘live’ what is learnt and apply it to everyday situations in the school community. Class teachers deliver the weekly lessons to their own classes. Teachers inform parents of the specific content of lessons in their half-termly curriculum letters.

Welcome to Modern Foreign Languages
Why do we learn modern foreign languages?
Our French curriculum aims to give children skills in three areas: oracy, literacy and intercultural understanding. Children are taught to view themselves as able to communicate and read in French and to have a sense of culture and lifestyle through discovering more about France and its people. This will lead to them being less insular and more outward-looking, broadening their horizons and fostering an ambitious spirit. Importantly, by viewing non-native teachers speaking the language and ‘walking the walk’, children are taught to see themselves as language learners in a similar way.

Welcome to Religious Education
Why do we learn Religious Education?
Our RE curriculum is based on an enquiry approach, making RE lessons exciting, engaging and thought-provoking. It promotes British values and enhances children’s learning and spiritual development. It encourages the celebration of diversity. It intends to help children to articulate and communicate their thoughts and to make them appreciate the experiences, beliefs and thoughts of those in their community and beyond.
Our approach
The curriculum is taught via a sequence of enquiry modules. Christianity is taught in every year group and learning about Christmas and Easter develops each year in a progressive way. Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism and Sikhism and also included. The Four Step Enquiry Model The key question for the enquiry is such that it demands an answer that weighs up ‘evidence’ and reaches a conclusion based on this. This necessitates children using their subject knowledge and applying it to the enquiry question, rather than this knowledge being an end in itself. The curriculum focuses on critical thinking skills, on personal reflection into the child’s own thoughts and feelings, on growing subject knowledge and nurturing spiritual development.
Parents/carers are able to withdraw their child from RE or collective worship.

Welcome to Music
Why do we learn music?
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement (The National Curriculum). At Brunel we believe in providing a music curriculum that allows our pupils to experience, learn and excel at this art form; where children have opportunities to perform, compose and develop a critical and thoughtful appreciation of the worldwide range of musical styles both from the past and in the present.
Our approach
Following the Ark Music Programme, all our children across the school engage with the vocal curriculum that is lead by qualified and experienced singing coaches. In Years 3, 4, 5 and 6, children also have Djembe and Ukulele lessons taught by specialist artists. Our music curriculum is further enhanced by enrichment activities, such as choirs, instrumental ensembles and special musical events that are held throughout the year.

Welcome to Art
Why do we learn art?
At Brunel, we aim to inspire creativity and develop knowledge and skills in our children so that they are confident to create their own works of art, craft and design. We teach about how art contributes to our culture of the world around them. Our art curriculum promotes spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical growth and development through creating opportunities and experiences of creating art through a variety of techniques and methods.
Our approach
At Ark Brunel, children are encouraged to evaluate their own artwork and that of other pupils, saying what they think and feel about it. They explore a range of artists and art styles, developing these influences into their own work. We encourage children to develop art through the way they interpret different pieces, artists and styles through observing, discussing and communicating what they see, feel and think through the use of colour, texture, form, pattern and different materials and processes. As pupils progress, they should be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design. They should also know how art and design both reflect and shape our history, and contribute to the culture, creativity and wealth of our nation.
Across the years 1-6, art is categorised into 5 important strands. Each unit will focus on a key strand linked to a topic theme. These strands are ‘Self-portraits’, ‘Drawing and Painting’, ‘Collage’, ‘Sculpture’, and ‘Printing’.

Welcome to Computing
Why do we learn computing?
Our computing curriculum ensures that children in all year groups enjoy a comprehensive programme of study that allows their creativity to flourish, devising expressive multi-media stories, games and pictures. It is aligned to the national Curriculum and EYFS framework. The overview facilitates teachers to achieve the very best outcomes, regardless of starting points. It exposes pupils to a wide variety of skills, experiences and poignant real-life scenarios which supports the notion of cultural capital; providing the foundations that lead to well-rounded global citizens.
Our approach
Children study a range of areas over the course of a year, including:
Lessons are progressive and 8 identified themes are planned over the course of Ks1 and KS2 which set foundations which are built upon in later years. For example, coding first features in Year 1 and features in each subsequent year, with learning being built upon each year. Earlier, in EYFS, children use technology to develop perseverance and resilience, develop fine motor skills and reflect on what may be beneficial or harmful to their health when discussing ‘screen time.’ They use technology to try new activities, developing their independence and a love of challenge. Artistic expression is developed through use of technology, with children having opportunities to explore and experiment with colour and form. Lessons can be undertaken in the computing room or in classrooms using tablets. There are 5 unscheduled weeks in KS1 to be used to reinforce learning as appropriate. In KS2, revision or learning of optional units may be undertaken as appropriate. Online safety is integral to the programme and children are taught a range of ways to ensure they are safe online.

Why do we learn design technology?
At Ark Brunel, the curriculum for design and technology aims to ensure that all pupils:
Our approach
Our design and technology curriculum which allows them to exercise their creativity through designing, constructing and making. The children are taught to combine their designing and making skills with knowledge and understanding in order to design and make a product. Skills are taught progressively to ensure that all children are able to learn and practise in order to develop as they move through the school. Evaluation is an integral part of the design process and allows children to adapt and improve their product, this is a key skill which they need throughout their life. Our design and technology curriculum follows the National Curriculum, promoting the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical growth and development through opportunities and experiences of designing, constructing and making. Through this curriculum, children are also able to combine practical skills and techniques with their understanding of social and environmental topics in order to reflect on and evaluate.

Welcome to English
Our English mission is to develop independent thinkers, critical readers, eloquent writers.
Why do we learn English?
At Brunel, we believe that a quality English curriculum should develop children’s love of reading, writing and discussion. We have a rigorous and well organised English curriculum that provides many purposeful opportunities for reading, writing and discussion.
Our approach
Our curriculum closely follows the aims of the National Curriculum for English 2014 to enable all children to:
read easily, fluently and with good understanding
appreciate our rich and varied literary heritage
demonstrating to others and participating in debate.

Welcome to Geography
Why do we learn geography?
At Brunel we aim to inspire pupils’ curiosity to know more about the world we live in. All Brunel children will leave primary school with a wide ranging and deep knowledge of the physical and human geography of the UK and the wider world, of key geographical terms, and skills such as fieldwork and map reading. We aim to equip pupils with the ability to ask perceptive questions, think critically, examine written sources and photographical evidence, and read maps with confidence using a range of mediums (atlases, grid references, symbols and keys, and digital maps).
Our approach
We focus on core geographical skills such as examining a wide range of sources, considering changes to the environment and the impact over time these changes have had, and building children’s locational knowledge of both their local area and the wider world. In their time at Ark Brunel, pupils will learn about the geography of their local area; the geography of the wider world; key human and physical features; and key map skills, such as understanding a grid reference. As a school, we have mapped out the significant locations of the world to ensure pupils obtain a balanced understanding of both the geography of their local area and the UK, as well as globally.

Welcome to History
Why do we learn history?
At Brunel we aim to inspire pupils’ curiosity to know more about the history of the world in which they live. All Brunel children will leave primary school with a wide ranging and deep knowledge of the past, of places and people and significant events through time. We aim to equip pupils with the ability to ask perceptive questions, think critically, weigh evidence, sift arguments, and develop perspective and judgement.
Our approach
We focus on core historical enquiry skills from the national curriculum such as: similarities and differences, continuity and change, significance, the impact of individuals and events, comparing and contrasting, and source analysis. From the beginning of KS1 through to the end of KS2, pupils are exposed to a wide range of historical periods across the globe. In their time at Ark Brunel, pupils will learn about global history alongside that of the British Isles; how nations have changed; and how Empires and civilisations have risen and fallen and the impact they left behind. As a school, we have mapped out significant People and Places of History – ensuring the sharing of knowledge from around the world.

Welcome to Maths
Why do we learn maths?
At Brunel, we intend to make maths learning meaningful and applicable. We believe that the mastery approach we use gives pupils deeper understanding and makes maths more enjoyable. We believe that academic success is a by-product of this approach. The key principles of conceptual understanding, language and communication, and mathematical thinking come together to give children the ability to apply these skills to solve problems, both now and in the future. Mathematical thinking permeates all avenues of life: this approach prepares children for the next phase in their education and ultimately, the world of work.
Our approach
Our curriculum uses Ark’s Maths Mastery, a fully resourced programme with regular opportunities for PD, using online tutorials and regular network meetings. Curriculum design means children revisit key learning regularly, helping them embed learning. In-built progression ensures that children have the prior knowledge that allows them to be successful. Resources for daily lessons allow teachers to focus on the mathematical thinking and less on time-consuming resource creation. This enables them to focus on making learning meaningful and challenging for all, providing scaffold and challenge. A wealth of additional resources support the daily maths lessons, including regular maths meetings to revisit areas of study and help children to commit key understanding and facts to long-term memory.

Welcome to Physical Education
Why do we learn physical education?
We have 3 main aims for PE at Ark Brunel:
To achieve this, we split the P.E. curriculum into 2 main areas: sports and fitness. The sport aspect of our curriculum teaches children key skills and movements which they can apply to a range of sports. These are then applied in a range of modified games such as football, tennis and basketball. The children also develop effective communication and teamwork skills. The fitness aspect of our curriculum teaches children how to be active to music and encourages children to lead healthy lifestyles. We also have a half termly focus on a different aspect of health. This helps children to make good choices and understand the effects of exercise on their bodies.
Every child is active
Children will be taught transferrable skills
Our approach
In Early years, the children build a foundation for their physical development through a range of activities both in and outside the classroom. In year 1 the children begin 2 PE sessions per week. These are structured with a clear warm up, activity and cool down. For example, the children play a game to warm up, learn a skill such as how to perform a forearm shot in tennis and then apply this in a short game. Then the children assess their progress and cool down. In KS1 the children engage in a variety of lessons, building their knowledge and vocabulary around sport and being healthy. They learn how to move their bodies in different ways and participate in sports such as athletics and basketball. They are introduced to the skills they will need such as throwing and catching, balancing and jumping. In KS2, the children build upon these skills. The children practise through a range of drills and matches. The teacher models and evaluates their progress throughout the lesson. The children practise in pairs and groups until they build up to a full match. They build on the knowledge and vocabulary they learnt in KS1 and use this to partake in PE lessons. PE lessons are fully accessible for all children including those with SEND. The skills and games are modelled carefully so each child understands what they are being asked to do. Vocabulary is clear and repeated so the children can begin to use this from an early age. The children leave primary school with a solid base in physical education. They know how to perform range of skills and can transfer these into different sports.

Welcome to Science
Why do we learn science?
At Brunel, we place great value on the importance of the teaching and learning of science to support all pupils to understand the world around them. We intend for pupils to have the knowledge they need to work scientifically in a meaningful way. We have a coherently planned and sequenced curriculum, which has been carefully designed and developed with the need of every child atits core.
Our approach
The curriculum is not only based on the minimum statutory requirements of the Science National Curriculum but has been developed to challenge and prepare them for the opportunities, responsibilities, and experiences of later life. We teach this by presenting the curriculum through a variety of engaging activities and a rich range of experiences. Children will become effective communicators in science by presenting their ideas and understanding in different ways. We believe that all pupils are entitled to understand how Science works in their own lives and within their local, national and global communities. We meet the needs of all pupils and make Science accessible to all children through a creative and engaging scheme of work. This enables us to support all pupils, regardless of need, in developing positive attitudes towards science, encouraging a natural curiosity in the pupils and a respect for the world around them. We aim to give our pupils the opportunities and the knowledge to become scientifically literate and encourage them to be the scientists of the future.
